excerpt: A recent qualitative study of 60 Buddhist meditators and meditation teachers applied 11 of 13 causality criteria and produced 60 categories of meditation-related experiences and 26 categories of influencing factors that may affect duration, distress, and impairment. The resulting codebook was being converted into a measurement tool for systematic assessment across studies and conditions.
overview: This item shows that adverse meditation-related experiences are being transformed from anecdotal reports into a structured research agenda. The evidence is qualitative and retrospective, so it does not estimate prevalence, but it supports the need for systematic safety assessment and testable hypotheses.
title: Adverse Experience Taxonomy
